hypothesis-level refutation: pre-registered falsification condition met. RSI(14) oversold-reversion on EURUSD H1, 12-bar horizon: expectancy negative in DEVELOPMENT (-16.95), VALIDATION (-19.43) and PURE_HOLDOUT (-27.81); no partition positive.

source-claim level: the RSI 70/30 overbought/oversold lore did not yield an exploitable edge in its tested operationalisation. Entry signal produced a 41.3% win rate where 50.7% was required at the frozen point's REALIZED payoff geometry -- short by 9.4 points.

MECHANICAL FINDING (transferable, not signal-specific): realized reward:risk is systematically BELOW nominal across the whole 360-point surface -- median 76% of nominal, falling to 53% at nominal RR 3.0 and rising to 99.7% at nominal RR 0.75; by holding cap, 64.2% (6 bars), 72.8% (12), 85.0% (24). Mechanism: a distant take-profit needs both time and a favourable path, and the max-holding-bar timer truncates would-be winners while the nearer stop still fires at full size. Consequence: the breakeven win rate a candidate must actually clear is HIGHER than its specified geometry implies (frozen point: 50.7% realized vs 42.9% nominal). Derived algebraically from per-point profit_factor and win_rate (realized_RR = PF*(1-wr)/wr), exact given those aggregates but an inference from them, not from per-trade avg_win/avg_loss records.

DIRECT PER-TRADE MEASUREMENT (not algebraic inference): realized reward:risk = 76.4629% of nominal on DEVELOPMENT+VALIDATION (74.2114% on PURE_HOLDOUT), confirming the Generation 4 post-mortem's algebraic estimate (77.1% at the frozen point) via genuine per-trade data.
failures.future_research_implication: A hypothesis that wants to use a distant take-profit should pair it with either no max-hold cap or a cap generous enough that MAX_HOLDING_PERIOD exits are rare, not with a tight cap that truncates most winners before they arrive.
failures.mechanism: Measured directly per exit reason on 646 DEVELOPMENT+VALIDATION trades: TAKE_PROFIT exits average +1.29R (near nominal); STOP_LOSS exits average -1.04R (slightly worse than nominal -1.0R from slippage); MAX_HOLDING_PERIOD exits average only +0.13R -- the time-out chops would-be winners down to a small fraction of the nominal target before they can reach it.
failures.prevention_rule: Before freezing a candidate with a max-holding-bar cap, check what fraction of the nominal reward the average MAX_HOLDING_PERIOD exit actually achieves in-sample; if it is a small fraction of 1R, the effective breakeven win rate is materially higher than the nominal-RR breakeven and the candidate should be evaluated against THAT bar, not the nominal one.
failures.scope: Transferable to ANY future candidate in this Factory using ATR-multiple take-profits with a max-holding-bar cap, regardless of entry signal -- the mechanism is about the exit geometry, not this RSI rule specifically.

failures.failure_reason: Independent signal-only measurement (no stop/target/max-hold involved): conditional 12-bar forward-return edge = 0.000095, which is smaller than the round-trip transaction cost expressed as a return fraction. Classified SIGNAL_FAILURE, not EXECUTION_FAILURE: even before any exit mechanics are applied, the entry signal carries no economically material edge.
failures.future_research_implication: A future RSI-family hypothesis at a DIFFERENT horizon or regime condition (e.g. HYP-000002, HYP-000003) is not pre-refuted by this finding, but should be measured with this same signal-only test before any execution layer is built around it.
failures.mechanism: RSI(14) oversold-reversion crossing has near-zero correlation with forward returns at a 12-bar horizon on EURUSD H1, measured directly from the price path with no trading-rule mechanics involved -- confirms Generation 4 post-mortem section 3's finding at nominal RR 0.75 (where geometry erosion is minimal) that the signal has no edge on its own.
failures.prevention_rule: Before formalizing an ATR-based execution layer around an entry signal, measure the signal's raw forward-return edge independent of any stop/target/hold, and compare it to round-trip transaction cost -- an edge below that floor cannot be rescued by exit-mechanics tuning.
failures.scope: Specific to RSI(14) crossing 30 from below, EURUSD H1, 12-bar horizon -- not a claim about RSI mechanisms generally, and not evidence about any other instrument/timeframe.

failures.failure_reason: CORRECTION to FAIL-000015 (miscategorised NEGATIVE_EXPECTANCY): this hypothesis had POSITIVE net expectancy +2.67 pips/trade on train but failed the t>=2.0 screening gate at t=0.99 with only n=130 trades. It is UNDERPOWERED, not unprofitable.
failures.future_research_implication: Do NOT re-test this family on the same window hoping for a different answer, and do NOT relax the t-gate to admit it. Two legitimate paths exist: (a) pool the same event mechanism across multiple correlated-but-distinct symbols to raise n without reusing the same observations, or (b) leave it dormant until more calendar time accumulates. Option (a) requires new instrument data the Factory does not currently hold.
failures.mechanism: Large weekend gaps (>8 pips) faded toward Friday close produced +2.67 pips/trade net over 130 train events (t=0.99). The per-trade effect clears the 1.1-pip cost by ~2.4x -- the only failure is statistical power: weekend gaps are ~52 events/year, so a 9.4-year train window yields ~130 qualifying events. Standard error is too large to reject the null at t>=2 regardless of how real the effect may be.
failures.prevention_rule: Before spending a test slot on an event-driven hypothesis, compute the expected event count over the available window (event_rate x years). If the projected n cannot reach t>=2.0 at the plausible effect size, the hypothesis is UNTESTABLE ON THIS DATA -- reject it at generation time as underpowered rather than consuming a test slot and a research budget unit to rediscover that.
failures.scope: EURUSD H1 weekend-gap events with |gap| > 8 pips. Applies to any low-frequency event-driven family: the sample-size ceiling is set by event frequency, not by data length.

failures.failure_reason: Across all 5 families, mean train cost-efficiency rose monotonically with horizon (roughly consistent with sqrt(horizon) scaling of gross movement against a fixed cost) -- but trade count n necessarily falls as horizon grows (non-overlapping trades), so statistical power falls in the same direction cost-efficiency rises. Every train-gate pass (5 of 243 evaluations) occurred at horizon>=12, and every one of those 5 failed validation (3 sign-flipped negative, 2 underpowered).
failures.future_research_implication: Horizon extension alone, on one instrument, cannot resolve the cost-vs-power tradeoff -- it only relocates it. Future cycles need EITHER (a) multi-instrument pooling to decouple n from horizon, or (b) a genuinely higher-frequency signal with more raw events per unit time so long-horizon holds still leave adequate n, or (c) a different cost structure (lower spread instrument) so shorter horizons already clear cost-efficiency without needing n-destroying long holds.
failures.mechanism: Cost amortization via horizon extension is real (confirms the premise) but structurally self-defeating on a single-symbol, single-window dataset: the same denominator shrinkage that improves cost-efficiency also destroys the sample size needed to trust the estimate.
failures.prevention_rule: Before sweeping horizons on a single instrument, compute projected n at each horizon (roughly bars_in_window / horizon, adjusted for signal frequency) and pre-reject horizons where the projected n cannot reach the power gate at any plausible effect size -- this would have eliminated horizon>=120 for every family in this sweep before spending the evaluations.
failures.scope: Applies to ANY single-instrument horizon-extension search on this ~9.5-year dev window -- not specific to any one family.

failures.failure_reason: Cycle 3 multi-asset sweep: 0/43 hypotheses across 6 instruments cleared train (t>=2.0) and internal validation (t>=1.5, n>=30) after the frozen per-symbol round-trip cost.
failures.future_research_implication: Next cycles must change the economics, not the sample: lower-cost execution, larger-effect event windows, or genuinely multi-leg structures whose gross effect scales past the cost floor.
failures.mechanism: Every surviving-in-gross H1 pattern the observatory found is smaller than the round-trip cost on every instrument tested. Widening the instrument cross-section multiplied the sample but did not change the sign of net expectancy: the cost floor, not the sample size, is the binding constraint.
failures.prevention_rule: Do not re-test single-instrument H1 price-pattern families by adding more instruments. Cross-sectional breadth does not defeat a cost floor; only a larger gross effect or a lower cost does.
failures.scope: H1 bars, 6 major/commodity instruments, retail-realistic cost. Says nothing about lower timeframes, other asset classes, or execution models with materially lower cost.
